---
pagetitle: "Peekbank | About"
title: "About Peekbank"
---

The Peekbank project aims to make developmental eye-tracking data more
accessible for sharing and reuse. We do this by reducing the amount of
preprocessing necessary to perform typical analyses and by storing data in
a common, tidy format that allows for easy cross-dataset comparisons.

We release new dated versions periodically to facilitate reproducibility
(see [Releases](docs.html#releases)), and support an API via the
[peekbankr](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/) R package, which lets
users access the data in Peekbank without writing queries.

Peekbank is open source and under active development. If you encounter a
problem, please file an issue in the
[GitHub Issues page](https://github.com/peekbank) of the appropriate
repository. If you would like to contact us directly, email us at
[peekbank-dev@lists.stanford.edu](mailto:peekbank-dev@lists.stanford.edu).

## About this site

The visualizations follow standard analysis conventions for
looking-while-listening data (Fernald, Zangl, Portillo, & Marchman, 2008):
proportion target looking among target-and-distractor looks; landing-time
reaction times on distractor-initial trials; onset-contingent looking
curves. Trials excluded by the contributing labs are included by default
(Peekbank archives all contributed data), and can be filtered with the
"Excluded trials" toggle. Everything is computed in your browser from
compact extracts of the current release; the full data live on
[Redivis](https://stanford.redivis.com/datasets/a3v0-3drqa89kg).

Built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org) and
[Observable](https://observablehq.com/plot/); source at
[peekbank/peekbank-datapage](https://github.com/peekbank/peekbank-datapage).
